name: Disorder of Melanin Metabolism

ethnicAssociations: More frequent in populations with higher consanguinity rates

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Biochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Melanin Metabolism Disorders

criteria.description: Presence of generalized or localized hypopigmentation of skin, hair, and eyes
Biochemical evidence of disrupted melanin biosynthesis pathways (e.g., tyrosinase activity deficiency)
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in melanin metabolism
Ophthalmological abnormalities such as nystagmus or reduced visual acuity
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of hypopigmentation, biochemical evidence of melanin synthesis disruption, and genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may require multidisciplinary evaluation including dermatology, ophthalmology, and genetics

pathognomonic.symptomName: Generalized hypopigmentation of skin and hair
searchTerms: generalized light skin and hair color
lack of pigmentation in skin and hair
light skin and iris showing light through
lack of pigment causing eye shine-through

pathognomonic.symptomName: Reduced or absent melanin pigment in retinal pigment epithelium
searchTerms: reduced pigment in eye's retina layer
sensitivity to light from pale iris
light skin patches with dark edges
hypopigmented areas bordered by darker skin

laboratory: Reduced or absent tyrosinase enzyme activity in melanocytes
Abnormal melanin content in skin biopsy
Elevated serum levels of melanin precursors in some subtypes
imaging: Optical coherence tomography showing retinal pigment epithelium hypopigmentation
MRI may show normal brain structure; occasionally mild hypomyelination
genetic: Pathogenic variants in TYR, OCA2, or other melanin metabolism-related genes
other: Electroretinogram abnormalities consistent with retinal dysfunction
Visual evoked potentials showing delayed conduction

distinguishingFeatures: Patchy skin involvement without systemic or ocular abnormalities
No genetic mutations in melanin biosynthesis genes
Primarily ocular involvement without generalized skin hypopigmentation

redFlags: Severe visual impairment in early childhood
Progressive neurological symptoms such as seizures
Rapid onset of extensive skin depigmentation
references: Orphanet: Disorder of Melanin Metabolism - ORPHA:352728
King RA, Hearing VJ. Molecular biology of albinism. Hum Mol Genet. 2001
Kruijt CC, et al. Clinical and molecular aspects of melanin metabolism disorders. J Invest Dermatol. 2019
